title: The New Sounds
notes: - Fluttery bebop. Not unlike Giant Steps, but still mellow, listenable. Miles already sounds like himself--aloof and cool. Sonny Rollins sounds like a tickled deity. 4.20/5 stars. Would revisit.

title: Young Man With A Horn
notes: - Slower, a bit more melancholy, but still drives. Yesterdays hits like a dart to the gut. Solid overall, would've taken more JJ on the bone. 8.6/12. Will come back to it when I’m feeling wistful.

title: Blue Period
notes: - Light, breezy blues and bebop, apparently recorded during the New Sounds sessions. Not particularly noteworthy but perfectly fine. Would pair well with a G&T on a spring afternoon. 6/9.420 trumpets.

title: The Compositions of Al Cohn
notes: - Sorry Al but I don’t love these compositions. Musty pudding. 2/6 snack packs.

title: Miles Davis Volume 2
notes: - A mix of hard bop and slow jams. The ballads didn’t really do it for me but I liked the fast songs. The compositions are interesting and Art Blakey thumps like a madman on the skins. 7/11 Arnies.

title: Miles Davis Volume 3
notes: - Alright now we’re talking. Hard bop. A little funkier. Definitely my favorite so far.  Could listen to “It Never Entered My Mind” > “Well You Needn’t” on loop for hours. Horace Silver is a stanky warlock on the keys. B+/100. Would recommend.

title: Miles Davis Quartet
notes: - Sunny. Lyrical. With only 4 guys playing at a time, you get a lot more Miles. Love the way he sounds on this one. Pure, unadulterated. Elemental even. 4/5 planeteers. Praise be to mother Gaia.

title: Miles Davis All Star Sextet
notes: - Cool, bluesy tune followed by a quickier, boppier number. Arranged sections are almost cartoonish but the solos are solid. Miles is in full stride. JJ finally gets some room to breathe. Lucky Thompson sounds so velvety I blushed. Low eighties out of a hundred.

title: Miles Davis Quintet
notes: - Sounds like 2am in a Greenwich Village basement. Miles has his signature smokey tone. Don’t know this sax man but was pleasantly surprised. Sounds like Paul Desmond—clear and sparkly. Horace Silver and Kenny Clarke serve as the perfect compliments. High 16/20. Will keep in the rotation.

title: Miles Davis with Sonny Rollins
notes: - An all time great musical bromance. Love the way Miles sounds playing these intricate, Sonny-composed tunes. Rollins himself soars. Feels like I’m riding no hands over the Williamsburg bridge. 8.999…/10. Classic.
